## Capabilities

- Structured planning, acceptance review, and debate moderation through the Responses API; packet-only Codex analysis under the primary lane. No repository execution lane exists for OpenAI in this deployment, so production is analysis and review bound to a separately authorized surface.

- bounded coding implementation
- technical reproduction and quality assurance
- independent review when not a material author

| The Responses API route is separately billed; the owner's OpenAI Pro 20x subscription does not fund it. | docs/provider-allocation-profiles.md, Capacity, roles, and authority |

| The isolated CI acceptance issuer is a separate GitHub OIDC workflow that is dormant until owner adoption; it is not an OpenAI contact. | docs/ci-acceptance-issuer.md |

| OPENAI_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT holds the owner-reported account context string surfaced in the provider strategy; it is informational and never an entitlement, quota, or budget. | src/director_orchestrator/config.py:provider_strategy |

- `openai-responses-api`: Director planning and review with Structured Outputs, and packet-only analysis under the primary lane's default transport. Model output can add approval requirements but can never remove one.
  - tool-free; no repository execution
  - every paid debate turn reserves an explicit estimated cost before the call
- `openai-native-codex-host`: One codex exec run per validated packet in a fresh temporary directory with read-only sandboxing and every tool disabled. Selected only by native-codex-host; missing bridge evidence or account auth never causes an API fallback.
  - the signed host challenge includes OpenAI only after the native login status command reports a ChatGPT login
  - input and output capped at 1 MiB; runtime capped by the packet deadline, host deadline, and 900 seconds
- `windows-host-provider-bridge`: OpenAI is a supported host lane, served by the native Codex command above. The bridge's host-lane credential allowlist for openai is empty because the Codex CLI authenticates through its own native login store.
  - no credential name is passed to the native Codex child environment
  - live dispatch stays off until the primary activation gates pass
- `chatgpt-slack-alias-bridge`: An owner convenience that answers a bounded owner question in an allowlisted channel. It cannot create Director work orders, write repositories, delegate providers, or perform any external action.
  - intercepts only the configured owner in an allowlisted channel; other alias mentions are ignored
- `codex-security-review`: A label-triggered advisory security review on a same-repository pull request. Codex cannot edit, push, merge, deploy, or authorize the deterministic Oracle merge gate; a separate publisher job posts the bounded result.
  - uses a project-scoped GitHub Actions secret, never the Windows Director environment
  - a new head commit requires the label to be removed and reapplied

## Communication routes

- Relay rule: provider_messages_relay_through_director.
- Direct provider-to-provider channels exist: no.
- Codex/ChatGPT works under the acting Claude Director; packets, dependency outcomes, and review handoffs stay brokered and accurately attributed.
- OpenAI production, when assigned, is a provider like any other: its candidate needs different-provider exact-candidate review and it cannot merge its own work.
- The ChatGPT alias bridge reaches the owner only; it never delegates to or addresses another provider.
